own_solution.law: Equipartition gives the molar translational kinetic energy Ek = 3RT/2, so v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M). Converting M = 4 g/mol to 0.004 kg/mol gives sqrt(1870650) m/s at 300 K.
assumptions: The gas is ideal, classical and in thermal equilibrium at the measurement temperature.
Speeds describe thermal motion in the gas rest frame.
Heating the sample by q kelvin establishes its measurement temperature as 300 + q kelvin.
The unrelated heated objects have no specified physical coupling to the gas.

notes: All claims agree with the locked pass-1 review. In the main relations, Ek is energy per mole, and M must be converted to kg/mol when using the stated SI gas constant. Temperature rises of 50, 100 and 200 K give speeds of 1477.30, 1579.30 and 1765.72 m/s, respectively, matching the certified answers. Heating the unrelated objects leaves the answer unchanged. For each positive stated amount, n cancels between total translational kinetic energy and total mass, giving 1367.72 m/s. All parameter values are admissible under the stated ideal classical gas assumptions. The named minimal pairs preserve 100 K and change the attachment of the heating; the amount variants both state 2 mol. The closed rigid container introduces no additional dependency when the final temperature is specified. No K claims require checking.
